structural_preflight.disclosure: Two independent structure-only enumerations checked the unchanged 54 profiles before registration. Neither selected actions, evaluated policy values, inspected mechanism effects nor ran native timing. No profile or parameter was changed using their results.

coverage: Enumerate all positive-probability current observations and every legal action prefix. Keep explicit terminating abstention. Deduplicate identical public states within a profile, but retain every action's complete successor distribution. Action branches have no probability law; probabilities must not be summed across alternative actions or interpreted as IID state samples.
evaluation: Persistently apply each controller's own policy at every later state, evaluated under the true environment law and the same dynamic external objective. Exact Fraction probabilities, Q32 ties-to-even arithmetic and nested conditional downside risk are used. Before the first observation, use the probability mean of root conditional values, rounded once, with no additional ex-ante risk transform. Report first-action regret and whole-policy regret separately.
pure_belief_intervention: At every decision prior-belief-only resets only belief_num/belief_den to the declared initial prior, then calls same-objective. Current request, signal, residency, resources and numeric preference rules remain unchanged. Preserve original and planning observations. The historical no-adaptation arm resets both belief and numeric preferences and is labeled a joint intervention.
factorial: Use dynamic-ndu, prior-belief-only, fixed-preference-ndu and joint no-adaptation to report belief effects at each preference setting, preference effects at each belief setting, and the difference-in-differences interaction. These are finite-model policy comparisons, not independent empirical samples or a unique NDU contribution.
fixed_reference: Evaluate all three complete fixed-action policies, including their original feasibility fallback, under the same ex-ante nested-risk objective. Select one policy per profile before any physical run; ties choose the smallest fixed action (-1, then 0, then 1). Never select a fixed action separately by state. Charge all candidate planning/evaluation and selection work. This known-law model-optimal fixed reference is distinct from the historical sample-selected fixed policy.
native_execution: For both native arms call model.plan with the original source-bound NativeValueBackend on every registered state, including every Bellman backup. No scalar substitution, oracle continuation substitution or favorable-state selection is allowed. Use one separately logged lazy native process per native arm per profile; retain startup, exchanges, failures and cleanup.
ordering: Use natural_profiles order, then the registered arm order, then sorted source-bound state identities. Timing is recorded as audit cost, not used to choose states, arms or outcomes.
failure_rule: Retain every planned state-arm cell and whole-policy denominator. Preserve failures and not-run reasons; do not evaluate an incomplete policy or retry with an enlarged budget. Each arm shares its original 20,000,000 search-expansion cap across all 54 profiles. Offline graph and policy-evaluation work are separately counted and timed.
scope: Offline known-law finite-model causal and whole-policy audit. No new physical workload cohort, training, gradient, general FBSDE, unique NDU superiority, full-lifecycle economic benefit or production activation is established.
